svg.title: Germany wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Trace selected wine regions along western river valleys and the southern German landscape. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Ahr. A small western river valley south of Bonn and north of the Mosel. 2: Mosel. Western Germany along the winding Mosel; its wine region also includes Saar and Ruwer vineyards. 3: Rheingau. A short Rhine corridor west of Wiesbaden. 4: Nahe. The Nahe valley southwest of the Rhine–Main confluence. 5: Rheinhessen. West of the Rhine, south of Mainz and north of the Pfalz. 6: Pfalz. A north–south western strip toward the French border. 7: Franken. Inland northern Bavaria, especially around the Main and Würzburg. 8: Württemberg. Southwestern Germany around the Neckar and its tributaries. 9: Baden. A long discontinuous southwestern region; the locator near Freiburg represents only part of its extent.

g.text: Dots: representative places · outlines: geography, not appellation boundaries
